beats.say: Every pipeline answer ends with one question.
How is it scheduled, retried, and backfilled?
beats.label: The question
beats.head: Scheduled, retried, backfilled?

beats.say: Three ideas answer it: what an orchestrator does, data intervals, and idempotent tasks.
beats.label: Track 8 · Orchestration

beats.say: First: what is an orchestrator for?
It starts tasks on time. It runs them in order. It retries failures. And it shows you what happened.
beats.label: Four jobs

beats.say: It should not do the heavy work itself. It tells Spark or the warehouse to do it.
beats.label: The rule
beats.head: It directs. It does not lift.

check.prompt: An Airflow run has the logical date of Monday, on a daily schedule. When does it start?
check.why: A run covers a data interval. It starts when the interval is complete.

beats.say: Second: the idea people get wrong in Airflow.
A daily run does not mean today. It covers one full day of data.
beats.label: Data interval
beats.head: A run covers an interval

beats.say: So the run for Monday starts after Monday ends. The data is complete then.
beats.label: When it runs
beats.head: Monday runs after Monday ends

beats.say: Use the interval dates in your queries. Never use the clock time of now.
beats.label: The habit
beats.head: Use the interval, not now()

check.prompt: Which task is safe to run again for the same day?
options: One that overwrites the partition of that day
check.why: An overwrite of the partition gives the same result on every run.

beats.say: Third: any run can run again.
A retry or a backfill runs the same task twice. The result must be the same.
beats.label: Idempotent
beats.head: Twice gives the same result

beats.say: An append adds the rows again. Now you have duplicates.
beats.label: The trap
beats.head: Append makes duplicates

beats.say: So overwrite the partition of that interval. Or use a merge on a key.
beats.label: The fix
beats.head: Overwrite the partition

beats.say: Last: Airflow, Prefect, or another tool?
Airflow is the standard, with a schedule and a graph you define first.
beats.label: Airflow
beats.head: The standard. Graph first.

beats.say: Prefect runs normal Python functions, and the flow can change while it runs.
beats.label: Prefect
beats.head: Plain Python, dynamic flows

beats.say: Quick recap of orchestration.
The orchestrator directs. A run covers an interval. And every task can run twice.
beats.label: Orchestration
items: It directs, it does not lift

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
